abstract: Electrophysiological research increasingly relies on complex analytical workflows, yet integrating methodological evidence, computational execution and reproducibility remains challenging. Here we introduce MLE EEG Toolbox, a framework for building a personal AI laboratory assistant for electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG) research. The toolbox integrates locally deployed AI, natural-language-guided analysis, literature retrieval and methodological comparison, and reproducible computational workflows. A constrained language model translates research instructions into validated, researcher-approved operations, while literature-informed guidance supports parameter selection and protocol reconstruction. Computational provenance enables transparent inspection and replay of analytical workflows. The assistant achieved action-selection accuracies of 85.6% for EEG and 95.5% for MEG, while 142 cross-platform tests demonstrated close numerical agreement. Applications to public EEG and MEG datasets illustrated integrated spectral, network, decoding and source analyses. Running on standard personal computers without external AI APIs or token charges, MLE EEG Toolbox provides an accessible, researcher-controlled environment that connects methodological knowledge with reproducible electrophysiological analysis.
